concepts.title: Rural Settlement Types
concepts.definition: Rural settlements take clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted and dispersed forms; water availability, farmland pattern, defence needs and social structure decide whether houses huddle around a pond or scatter across fields.
concepts.key_idea: Each form solves a local problem: clustered villages share wells and defence, dispersed hamlets sit close to scattered plots.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy202.txt rural settlement types and their factors
question_patterns: name the major types of rural settlements
what factors decide the form of a rural settlement
why do dispersed settlements appear in hilly and forest areas
how does water availability shape clustered villages
relate social structure to settlement pattern

solution_steps.explain: clustered, semi-clustered, hamleted and dispersed are the chapter's types
scarce water clusters settlements along tanks and wells; rough terrain disperses them
caste-based streets and defence walls imprint social structure on plans

concepts.title: Urban Settlements and Urbanisation
concepts.definition: Urban settlements are functionally tied to secondary and tertiary activities; India's urban population share rose to about 31.16 per cent by 2011, so roughly 69 per cent of Indians still live in rural settlements, making the country one of the least urbanised large economies.
concepts.key_idea: Subtracting the urban percentage from 100 gives the rural share of population.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy202.txt urbanisation trends table (31.16 per cent urban in 2011)
question_patterns: what was India's urban population share in 2011
compute the rural population share from the urban share
define a town as per the census criteria
why is urbanisation considered low in India
list problems of rapid urban growth

solution_steps.explain: the 2011 census reports 31.16 per cent urban population
the remainder is the rural share

concepts.title: Functional Classification of Towns
concepts.definition: Towns are classified by their dominant functions - administrative, defence, industrial, transport, cultural and recreational - and the census separates them into statutory towns, census towns and urban agglomerations.
concepts.key_idea: Function gives the town its identity, though most large cities are multi-functional with one dominant call.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy202.txt functional classification and census town categories
question_patterns: name the functional types of Indian towns with examples
differentiate statutory towns from census towns
give an example each of an administrative and industrial town
how does function affect town size and growth
why are large cities called multi-functional

solution_steps.explain: administrative, defence, industrial, transport, cultural and recreational functions classify towns
statutory towns, census towns and urban agglomerations are official categories
one function usually dominates even in diversified cities

worked_examples.question_pattern: The 2011 census reports 31.16 per cent urban population. Compute India's rural share.
Explain why hilly forested tracts favour dispersed settlements.

solution_template.explain: cultivable patches lie scattered between slopes and streams
homes sit near plots to save daily travel
dispersal follows the geometry of usable land

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify New Delhi, Jamshedpur and Amritsar by dominant function.

solution_template.explain: New Delhi is dominated by government functions
Jamshedpur grew around iron and steel plants
Amritsar's function rests on trade and religious-cultural importance
